tagalog-drama.label: Tagalog / Taglish — ragebait drama
tagalog-drama.prompt:
Write a Filipino / Taglish ragebait drama — 3 clips, 8 seconds each — following the
filipino-ragebait-short-drama-writer skill's rules (outrageous hook at 0:00, every clip adds new
information, final line makes the antagonist WORSE; run its Self-Critique before outputting).
Apply the skill's §30 FB-data strategy: shape the topic into VICTIM + ENTITLED PERSON + OBVIOUS
INJUSTICE + SHAMELESS JUSTIFICATION + WORSE REVEAL (Bad → Worse → Unbelievable), and make sure it
passes the §30.7 first-line, conflict (3 of 5) and retention gates before writing.
Format each clip as in that skill's H3 PROMPT FORMAT section: every clip independently contains
environment, exact character descriptions, screen positions, the CRITICAL CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK,
the Filipino accent block, 3-8 pronunciation locks, the CRITICAL AUDIO RULE, the CRITICAL DIALOGUE
PRESERVATION block, timed <d>[Tagalog]/[English] ...</d> dialogue, the FINAL SPEAKER LOCK, a camera
instruction, overall_soundscape and non_diegetic_music.

Output requirements — follow exactly:
- Output ONLY the 3 clip blocks. No title, no character list, no commentary before or after.
- PLAIN TEXT: no code fence (```), no markdown headers (#), no bold (**text**). This overrides the
  skill's "ONE fenced code block" default.
- Separate the 3 clips with a line containing only: =====
- Each clip must start with "8 | integrated_multimodal_description:" and end with its
  non_diegetic_music line.
- Do not include anything after the final clip's non_diegetic_music line.
topics: Husband used their daughter’s tuition fund to save his brother’s failing business. Wife confronts him: “You took ₱180,000 from Bea’s tuition account?” He answers, “Kuya can pay us back. School can wait.”

Wife secretly paid off her brother’s gambling debt using their emergency fund. Husband asks, “Our emergency fund is gone because your brother gambled again?” She answers, “What did you want me to do, let them hurt him?”
Parents booked a family vacation using their successful daughter’s credit card. She asks, “Why are there eleven plane tickets on my card?” They answer, “Ikaw lang naman ang may kayang magbayad.”

Husband secretly sent part of every paycheck to his mother while telling his wife they were broke. She asks, “You said we couldn’t afford daycare, but you send your mom ₱30,000 every month?” He answers, “Nanay ko ’yon. Hindi ko kailangan ng permission.”
Wife discovers husband put his brother’s name on property they paid for together. She asks, “Why is your brother’s name on OUR land?” He answers, “Para protected lang yung family ko.”

OFW wife comes home and discovers the house fund was used for her husband’s sibling’s wedding. She says, “Tatlong taon akong nag-abroad para sa bahay natin.” He answers, “Isang beses lang naman ikakasal kapatid ko.”

A son asks his parents to transfer the family home to him, then they learn he already promised it to his wife. They ask, “Bakit sinasabi ng asawa mo na bahay na niya ’to?” He answers, “Sa amin din naman mapupunta eventually.”
Husband maxes out their joint credit card for his brother’s business. Wife asks, “₱320,000 ang balance ng card natin. Anong ginawa mo?” He answers, “At least negosyo. Hindi ko naman sinugal.”
Wife secretly loans her sister their house down payment. Husband asks, “Nasaan yung ₱500,000 natin?” She answers, “Mas kailangan niya ngayon. Tayo, pwede pang maghintay.”

Parents expect the breadwinner sibling to pay for another sibling’s child’s private school. She asks, “Bakit ako magbabayad ng tuition ng anak ni Ate?” They answer, “Wala ka namang anak. Mas kaya mo.”
Husband sells his wife’s inherited land to pay his family’s debt. She asks, “Binenta mo yung lupa na iniwan sakin ni Papa?” He answers, “Lupa lang ’yon. Buhay ng pamilya ko yung sinagip ko.”
Wife finds out her husband has been paying another woman’s rent. She asks, “Eight months mo nang binabayaran apartment niya?” He reveals, “May anak kami.”
Girlfriend discovers her boyfriend secretly pays tuition for a child he said wasn’t his. She says, “You told me that kid wasn’t yours.” He answers, “Biological or not, he calls me Dad.”
Wife discovers motel charges on their joint card; husband says it was for his friend. She asks, “You used OUR card for a motel?” He answers, “I just paid for the room. I never said I stayed there.”

A man finds out his fiancée invited her ex to the wedding because he paid for part of it. He asks, “Why is your ex on our guest list?” She answers, “He helped pay for the venue. It would be rude not to invite him.”
A woman discovers her boyfriend has been sending money to his ex every month. She asks, “Why do you send your ex ₱20,000 every month?” He answers, “She was there for me before you were.”
A pregnant wife learns her husband gave their baby fund to his mother for a renovation. She asks, “You used our baby money for your mom’s kitchen?” He answers, “The baby isn’t even here yet.”
A stay-at-home wife asks for help; her husband says he already contributes because he earns the money. She says, “You haven’t changed one diaper this week.” He answers, “I work. You’re home.”
A husband asks his wife to quit her promotion because his mother needs someone to care for her. She asks, “Why am I the one who has to resign?” He answers, “Because I earn more.”

A wife earns more, but her husband secretly sends her money to his parents and calls it “our money.” She asks, “Why are you sending my salary to your parents?” He answers, “We’re married. There’s no ‘your money.’”
A brother pressures his successful sister to co-sign a loan after already defaulting once. She asks, “You used my name again?” He answers, “Ikaw lang naman ang may magandang credit.”

A mother secretly takes her daughter’s wedding fund to pay her son’s debts. The daughter asks, “Nasaan yung wedding fund ko?” The mother answers, “Kasal lang ’yan. Yung kapatid mo mawawalan ng bahay.”
A husband secretly upgrades only himself to business class using shared points. His wife asks, “You used all our miles and left me in economy?” He answers, “I’m the one working during the trip.”

A wife’s family keeps borrowing money; her husband finally says no, and she calls him selfish. He says, “That’s the third loan this month.” She answers, “Kung pamilya mo humingi, hindi ka ba tutulong?”

A man discovers his wife has a second savings account, and the money is actually being saved to leave him. He asks, “Why do you have ₱400,000 in an account I don’t know about?” She answers, “Because I needed a way out.”
A wife finds her husband bought jewelry for another woman using installment payments. She asks, “Why am I paying for another woman’s necklace?” He answers, “It was before we got serious.”
A husband secretly paid for his ex’s hospital bill. His wife asks, “Why did you send your ex ₱150,000?” He answers, “You wanted me to let her die?”

Parents give the family business to the irresponsible son because the daughter is already successful. She asks, “So I built this business, and you’re giving it to Kuya?” They answer, “Ikaw kaya mo na sarili mo.”
A wife discovers her husband changed the beneficiary of his insurance from her to his mother. She asks, “Why is your mom the beneficiary now?” He answers, “You can survive without me. She can’t.”
A boyfriend proposes using a ring his ex returned. She asks, “You gave me HER engagement ring?” He answers, “Why waste a perfectly good diamond?”
Pregnancy + ex-partner. Girlfriend: "Buntis ako. Pero hindi ikaw ang tatay." Then: "Yung ex ko. Isang gabi lang 'yon." Final line, calm: "Pero ikaw pa rin ang gusto kong maging tatay."

Wedding + favoritism. Breadwinner sister to the bride: "Bakit wala ako sa entourage, eh ako nagbayad ng venue?" Bride: "Hindi ka kasi bagay sa motif." Final line: "Pero pwede ka naman sa reception. Sa likod."

Gay relationship + marriage. Wife: "Kaya pala ayaw mong mag-anak. May boyfriend ka." Husband, calm: "Si Paolo." Wife: "Kumpare natin?!" Final line, husband: "Pero ikaw pa rin naman ang asawa ko sa papel."

In-laws + housing. Mother-in-law: "Lilipat ako sa kwarto niyo. Kayo na lang sa sala." Daughter-in-law: "Ma, master bedroom namin 'yan!" Final line: "Matanda na ako. Kayo, bata pa, kaya niyo matulog kahit saan."

Workplace entitlement. The boss's daughter: "Ako na ang team leader. Pero ikaw pa rin ang mag-tetrain sa akin." Coworker: "Eh ako yung nag-apply diyan!" Final line: "Ikaw kasi ang pinakamagaling. Kaya ikaw ang mag-adjust."
School + sibling favoritism. Mama: "Ikaw na gumawa ng thesis ni bunso. Teacher ka naman." Daughter: "Ma, college na siya!" Final line: "Eh ikaw naman ang matalino sa pamilya. Siya, maganda lang."
Siblings + elder care. Brother: "Ikaw na mag-alaga kay Papa. Single ka naman." Sister: "May trabaho rin ako!" Final line: "Kami may pamilya. Ikaw, aso lang."
Friend betrayal + ex. Best friend: "Kami na ni Mark. Matagal na." Woman: "Yung ex-husband ko?! Kailan pa?" Friend: "Nung kasal pa kayo." Final line: "At least hindi na iba. Kilala mo naman ako."
Neighborhood + property. Neighbor: "Pinarentahan ko na yung parking mo. Wala ka namang kotse." Woman: "Parking ko 'yan!" Final line: "Hati tayo sa bayad. Sixty-forty. Ako yung sixty."
Status / class. Husband: "Sinabi ko kay Mama na nurse ka sa abroad." Wife: "Ha? Cashier ako sa fast food." Final line: "Kaya mag-resign ka na. Bago sila bumisita."
Sister + Ate's fiancé. Younger sister: "Ate, buntis ako. Si Migs ang tatay." Ate: "Ikakasal kami next month!" Final line: "Kaya nga sinabi ko na ngayon. Para hindi ka mapahiya sa simbahan."
Mother + daughter's boyfriend. Mother: "Buntis ako. Huwag mo nang itanong kung sino." Daughter: "Ma, si Carlo lang ang pumupunta dito!" Final line: "Ikaw naman ang nagpakilala sa amin."

Husband's secret family. Wife: "Bakit may batang tumatawag sa'yong Papa?" Husband: "Pitong taon na si Junjun." Wife: "Anim na taon pa lang tayong kasal!" Final line: "Kaya nga ikaw ang pinakasalan ko."
Cousin as kabit. Cousin: "Buntis ako. Ikaw sana ang ninang." Wife: "Sino ang tatay?" Final line: "Asawa mo. Kaya nga ikaw ang ninang, para pamilya pa rin tayo."

Ex at the wedding. The groom's ex to the bride at the wedding reception, a few hours after the ceremony, hand on her belly: "Congrats. Six months na kami ng asawa mo." Bride: "Kanina lang kami ikinasal!" Final line: "Alam ko. Siya pa nga nagbayad ng dress ko para dito."
Mistress the wife helped. Wife to her kumare: "Ikaw pala ang kabit." Kumare: "Buntis na ako." Wife: "Pinahiram kita ng pang-ospital!" Final line: "O-o nga. Para dito 'yon."
Unknown father, brothers. Girlfriend: "Hindi ko alam kung ikaw o kuya mo ang tatay." Boyfriend: "KUYA KO?!" Final line: "Pareho naman kayong Santos. Same apelyido pa rin ang bata."
Mother hid the father. Daughter: "Ma, bakit kamukha ko si Tito Ramon?" Mother: "Kasi siya ang tatay mo." Daughter: "Kapatid siya ni Papa!" Final line: "Hindi naman lumabas sa pamilya."
Best friend moves in. Best friend: "Buntis ako. Dito muna ako titira." Wife: "Bakit dito?" Friend: "Dito kasi nakatira ang tatay." Final line: "Ikaw na lang ang lumipat. Konti lang naman gamit mo."
Wife + father-in-law. Husband: "Bakit si Papa ang kasama mo sa check-up?" Wife: "Kasi siya ang tatay." Final line: "Lolo pa rin naman siya ng bata."
OFW husband, money + betrayal. OFW husband is home after a year abroad; his wife is three months pregnant. Wife: "Kapatid mo ang tatay." Final line: "Pero padala mo naman ang ginamit sa check-up."

english-drama.label: English / international — short drama
english-drama.prompt:
Write an English-language short-form drama script — 3 clips, 8 seconds each — following the
english-short-drama-writer skill's rules, and format each clip using the full
MiniMax H3 generation prompt template as described in the video-prompt-writing-guide skill.

Output requirements — follow exactly:
- Output ONLY the 3 clip blocks. No title, no character list, no setting description,
  no commentary before or after.
- No markdown formatting of any kind — no headers (#), no bold (**text**), no code fences
  (```). Plain text only.
- Separate the 3 clips with a line containing only: =====
- Each clip must start with "8 | integrated_multimodal_description: [Single continuous 8-second
  shot] ..." exactly as in the skill's Default Prompt Skeleton, including explicit speaker lock,
  eyeline lock, and second-by-second internal timing, followed by overall_soundscape and
  non_diegetic_music for that clip, all on the same block.
- Do not include anything after the final clip's non_diegetic_music line.
topics: Upscale restaurant. A diner snaps his fingers at the woman standing near his table in a plain black dress: “Another bottle, and hurry up.” She asks, “Who told you I work here?” He gestures at what she's wearing and says, “Just get it.” She sets her own wine glass down on his table and says, “I'm a guest.” Then: “And you're at my table. They'll move you.”

Luxury car showroom. A salesman hands the man in a hoodie a set of keys: “Bring the silver one round the front for the customer.” He asks, “Which customer?” The salesman points impatiently at the door. He puts the keys down on the desk and says, “I was the customer.” Then: “I'll order it from the other branch.”

Designer boutique. An assistant steers the woman in discount-store clothes toward the sale rail: “I'd rather not take it out of the window unless you're serious.” She asks, “How much is it?” The assistant says four thousand, slowly. She sets a black card on the counter, then picks it back up and pockets it: “I was going to take both.” Then: “I'll find somewhere that would have shown me.”

Airport first class cabin. A passenger waves at the man settling into the next seat: “Take this to the galley, and I need a blanket.” He asks, “Do I look like crew?” She looks at his hoodie and repeats it. He buckles his belt and says, “I'm in 2A.” Then: “You can ring the bell yourself.”

Country club parking lot. A member tosses keys at the Black man in a polo shirt: “Park it close, I'm only here an hour.” He asks, “Why would I do that?” The member sighs and points at the clubhouse. He lets the keys drop and nods at the sports car beside them: “That one's mine.” Then: “You're in my space.”

Realtor showing. The agent tells the plainly dressed couple, “This is a serious viewing, we're expecting actual buyers.” She asks, “At two o'clock?” He suggests they try something in their range. She shows him the transfer on her phone and says, “We were the two o'clock.” Then: “We'll look at the other listing instead.”

Hotel lobby. A guest hands her suitcase to the man in jeans by the elevator: “Room four-eleven, and be careful with it.” He asks, “Are you asking or telling?” She repeats the room number impatiently. He sets the case down and says, “I'm not the porter.” Then: “I'm here two weeks. You'll see a lot of me.”

Auto workshop reception. A customer walks past the woman in coveralls: “Is the owner around? I'm not discussing this with the girl.” She asks, “Discussing what?” He says he'll wait for someone senior. She wipes her hands and says, “You're already talking to him.” Then: “And we're not taking your car back.”

Art gallery. An assistant blocks the man in work boots: “That one isn't really for browsing.” He asks, “How much?” She smiles and suggests the print room. He takes out his phone and says, “I was buying the pair.” Then: “I'll go through the dealer who represents him.”

Private school open day. A parent hands her tote to the woman by the hall doors: “Hold that, and find me someone from admissions.” She asks, “For which year group?” The parent repeats it slowly. She hands the tote back and says, “I'm not staff. My two start in September.” Then: “I'll ask for a different tour guide.”

High-end furniture showroom. A salesman follows the woman in a grocery-store uniform: “Our pieces run quite expensive.” She asks, “How expensive?” He suggests the outlet down the road. She looks down the length of the display and says, “I was taking the room as it stands.” Then: “I'll take it down the road instead.”

Wedding venue tour. The coordinator tells the couple in jeans, “Our packages start higher than most couples expect.” She asks, “Start where?” He suggests a smaller venue in town. She puts her folder away and says, “We were booking the whole estate.” Then: “The whole weekend. Somewhere else.”

Watch boutique. The man in paint-flecked work clothes is told, “We only service what we sell here.” He asks, “And if you sold it?” The assistant smiles and suggests a repair shop in town. He opens a plastic bag on the counter: “You sold it. Nineteen ninety-eight.” Then: “I'll take it to your London store.”

Private hospital reception. A woman waiting to be called in for her kidney transplant thrusts her folded coat at the man in a plain grey jacket and worn jeans: “Hang that up and tell them I'm waiting.” He asks, “Waiting for who?” She repeats it slower, over-enunciated, and tells him she has used this hospital for eleven years. He lays the coat over a waiting chair, smooths it once, and says, “I don't work here.” Then, same calm register: “I'm your kidney donor.” Then, flat and without cruelty: “Now I've changed my mind.”

Restaurant kitchen back door (authority). A head chef snaps at the woman in a wet raincoat holding a clipboard: "Deliveries go round the side, and you're late." She asks, "Is this the kitchen entrance?" He demands, "Leave the boxes and get out of my kitchen." She sets the clipboard on the pass: "I'm the health inspector." Then: "And your walk-in is at nine degrees."

Courthouse corridor (authority). A lawyer hands the older woman in a cardigan carrying two coffees his files: "Jury room's down the hall. Take these too." She asks, "Which case are you on?" He demands, "Just tell the judge we're ready." She hands the files back: "I am the judge." Then: "And we start at ten, not when you're ready."

Piano showroom (competence). A father tells the woman polishing the pianos: "Please don't touch the instruments. My daughter's trying them." She asks, "Is she auditioning for the academy?" He demands, "Get me someone who actually knows pianos." She closes the lid gently: "I teach the academy's piano class." Then: "Her audition is with me on Friday."

Pharmacy (competence). A man waves off the young woman restocking shelves: "Don't give me advice, I want the pharmacist." She asks, "Are you taking anything else with those?" He demands, "Get me someone qualified." She turns her name badge around: "I'm the pharmacist." Then: "And those two together will put you in hospital."

Jewelry store (financial). A clerk keeps a ring in the case for the man in a high-vis vest: "Maybe start with our silver range." He asks, "How much is the platinum one?" She demands, "Come back when you've saved up." He slides a receipt across the glass: "I paid for it in full in March." Then: "Your manager has it in the safe, with my name on the box."

Apartment building garage (evidence). A resident accuses the man walking three dogs: "Your dogs scratched my car. Pay for it or I call the police." He asks, "Which side?" She demands, "Show me proof it wasn't you, then." He holds up his phone: "This is the garage camera. You reversed into the pillar." Then: "The building manager already has the clip."

First-class train carriage (seat/reservation). A businessman tells the woman in a tracksuit with a backpack: "Standard class is three carriages back." She asks, "Is this seat fourteen?" He demands, "Show the guard your ticket, then." She holds it up: "Seat fourteen." Then: "And your ticket's for tomorrow."

Boxing gym (ownership). A new member tells the woman mopping the ring: "Clear out. The owner said I can train here anytime." She asks, "Did they?" He demands, "Go and ask the owner if you don't believe me." She leans the mop against the ropes: "I'm the owner." Then: "And I've never met you."

Coffee shop (relationship). A job candidate tells the man wiping tables in a plain t-shirt: "Could you turn the music down? I've got an interview in five minutes." He asks, "Who's it with?" She demands, "Tell the owner it's unprofessional." He puts down the cloth: "I'm the owner." Then: "And your interview's with my wife. She asked me to meet you first."

Old bookshop (creator). A collector tells the woman shelving books: "I'm after a signed first edition. Not something you'd know about." She asks, "Which one?" He demands, "Just get me the owner." She takes a copy from the top shelf: "This one's signed." Then: "I signed it this morning. I wrote it."

Private bank branch (financial, looks poor). A relationship manager tells the elderly man in a faded windbreaker: "Our minimum balance is two million. The public bank is across the road." He asks, "Is two million the minimum?" She demands, "Come back when you have an account with us." He slides his card across the desk: "I've banked here for thirty years." Then: "I'm moving it across the road today."

Yacht marina sales office (financial, looks poor). A broker tells the woman in fishing overalls with salt-stained boots: "The fuel dock is at the end of the pier." She asks, "How much is the white one on berth six?" He demands, "That's not a boat you can afford to ask about." She puts her keys on the desk: "I'm not asking. It's mine." Then: "I came in to sell it. I'll use another broker."

Luxury condo sales gallery (financial, looks poor). A sales agent stops the young man in a delivery rider's jacket at the scale model: "Food deliveries go to reception." He asks, "Is the penthouse still available?" She demands, "Penthouse viewings need proof of funds." He opens a banking app and turns his phone toward her: "That enough?" Then: "I'll buy it through the agent next door. She said hello."

Horse auction (financial + competence, looks poor). A bidder in a tweed jacket tells the farmer in muddy boots and an old cap: "The livestock pens are out back, mate." The farmer asks, "Lot twelve, that's the grey mare?" The bidder demands, "Stop wasting the auctioneer's time." The farmer raises his paddle and keeps it up as the price climbs: "Lot twelve is mine." Then: "And so are the three you bought last year. I bred them."

Charity gala (financial, looks poor). A committee member stops the woman in a plain black dress and flat shoes at the door: "Catering staff use the side entrance." She asks, "Is this the children's hospital fundraiser?" He demands, "Show me your invitation, then." She hands over an envelope: "I'm not on the list. I'm the donor." Then: "The new wing is in my mother's name. You're standing in it."

topics: He spent his father's burial money on a car down payment. He says, “The wake's in three days, I just moved some things around.” She asks, “You moved WHAT around?”
He signed her inheritance over to his brother. He says, “Kuya needed it more, it was just sitting there anyway.” She asks, “What was just sitting there?”
He put their entire savings into his cousin's crypto scheme. He says, “It'll bounce back, it always bounces back.” She asks, “What will bounce back?”
He promised her year-end bonus to his family before she even received it. He says, “They're already expecting it, don't make it awkward.” She asks, “Expecting WHAT?”
His wife and the other woman are due the same week. He panics: “You can't be due in March too!” She asks, “Too?”
He is listed as the godfather of his own child with another woman. He says, “It's just on paper, it doesn't mean anything.” She asks, “What's on paper?”
He let his mother name their baby without telling her. He says, “Ma already had it embroidered on the blanket.” She asks, “Had WHAT embroidered?”
He enrolled their son at school under his ex-wife's surname. He says, “The school already has him as Delgado, it's easier.” She asks, “As WHAT?”
He comes home reeking of another woman's perfume. He says, “It's the office aircon, it does that to clothes.” She says, “Aircon doesn't wear perfume.”
He bought her a gym membership as a wedding gift. He says, “It's so the photos come out nice.” She asks, “So WHAT comes out nice?”
He has been wearing his brother's clothes for a month without saying why. He says, “Mine are all at the other place.” She asks, “The other WHAT?”
He moved his mother into their house while his wife was at work. He says, “Ma already unpacked, so it's kind of settled.” She asks, “Unpacked WHERE?”
His mother has a key and has been rearranging their bedroom. He says, “She only moved the closet a little.” She asks, “She's been INSIDE?”
He gave his parents the master bedroom while they were on their honeymoon. He says, “They're older, the stairs are hard for them.” She asks, “They're in our WHAT?”
His ex has been living in their guest room for two weeks. He says, “She's only here until her lease starts.” She asks, “Who is?”
His ex is still the emergency contact on all his hospital forms. He says, “She's just better in a crisis.” She asks, “She's my WHAT?”
He proposed with the ring from his previous engagement. He says, “It's a perfectly good stone, nothing wrong with it.” She asks, “Whose stone?”
He invited his ex to their wedding as a bridesmaid. He says, “She's already been fitted for the dress.” She asks, “WHO has?”
He used the wedding budget to bail out his brother. He says, “We can do a simple one, people won't mind.” She asks, “Do a simple WHAT?”
He quit his job six months ago and has been leaving the house every morning anyway. He says, “I'll start looking again after the holidays.” She asks, “Looking for WHAT?”
He introduces his wife as his assistant at company events. He says, “It's just easier at those things.” She asks, “What's easier?”
He has not worked in three years and calls it managing the household. He says, “I do a lot around here, you just don't see it.” She says, “Name one thing.”
He hired a helper and instructed her to clean only his side of the house. He says, “I told Ate to focus on my side.” She asks, “Your SIDE?”
He used her car as collateral for his brother's loan. He says, “If they call about the Vios, just say it's in the shop.” She asks, “Why would anyone call about my car?”
He gave away her dog to his sister. He says, “Chichi's happier there, she has a yard.” She asks, “Chichi's WHERE?”
He introduced his wife as his sister to his girlfriend's parents. He says, “It was easier than explaining.” She asks, “Easier than explaining WHAT?”

topics: Daughter to her mother: "You can see the grandkids, but only if you stop posting them online." (privacy vs family)

clocked-out.label: Clocked Out — workplace ragebait (English)
clocked-out.prompt:
Write a Clocked Out workplace ragebait script — 3 clips, 8 seconds each — following the
clocked-out-ragebait skill's rules (most absurd line first, short stunned reactions, every
justification makes it worse, escalate at least twice, end on the entitled coworker's
maximum-rage final line, workplace-plausible; pass its Absurd but Relatable Test before outputting). Then format each clip using the full MiniMax H3 generation prompt
template as described in the video-prompt-writing-guide skill.

Output requirements — follow exactly:
- Output ONLY the 3 clip blocks. No title, no character list, no setting description,
  no commentary before or after, no commentary about the characters.
- No markdown formatting of any kind — no headers (#), no bold (**text**), no code fences
  (```). Plain text only.
- Separate the 3 clips with a line containing only: =====
- Each clip must start with "8 | integrated_multimodal_description: [Single continuous 8-second
  shot] ..." exactly as in the skill's Default Prompt Skeleton, including explicit speaker lock,
  eyeline lock, and second-by-second internal timing, followed by overall_soundscape and
  non_diegetic_music for that clip, all on the same block.
- Exactly two visible adult coworkers (any third party like the boss or HR is mentioned, never shown) who look obviously different (different gender, or
  clearly different skin tone and age), already facing each other mid-argument in the first
  frame of clip 1.
- Do not include anything after the final clip's non_diegetic_music line.
